Designing a fragrance store around the way people choose

How NURA’s storefront uses scent notes, formats, and a shopping bag to make a fragrance easier to choose online.

Webly · 9 November 2026 · Retail design · 1 min read

Give the collection a visual identity

NURA by Bin Sadhik already had a recognisable emerald and gold identity. The website carries those colours into the storefront, with a dark backdrop and large type so the product photography can lead. Consistent product presentation helps shoppers compare items while keeping the character of the brand.

Describe what an image can’t show

Fragrance photography sets the tone. Scent notes and product information help someone decide if a perfume is for them. Keep those details easy to scan and present perfume and concentrated oil as distinct formats. Give size and quantity their own controls before the shopper adds an item to the bag.

Keep the choices visible at the handoff

NURA uses a shopping bag before the move to WhatsApp. That gives a visitor one more chance to check the format, size, and quantity. When a store uses messaging to take orders, label the transition clearly and explain what the business will confirm in the conversation.
